title: Support Overage Invoicing on a Building Automation Service Plan and the Office Entry that Raises It
content:
# Support Overage Invoicing on a Building Automation Service Plan and the Office Entry that Raises It

## The charge

Controls support work that a plan's included support hours do not cover is invoiced to the building owner as a support overage on that plan under the Building Automation Service Plans. The support overage is raised as one charge at the handling day covering the twelve months to it rather than month by month, and is periodised to the calendar month in which it is raised.

## Raising it

The office entry that raises the charge is an agent-side tool the desk unlocks and then calls: `charge_controls_support_overage_c0d5009e`. One call raises one support overage line on a new office invoice against the named plan; the amount is added to what the owner owes under that plan, so the plan's outstanding balance rises by exactly that amount and the new charge appears in the plan's billing history at the building named, periodised to the calendar month in which it is raised. The owner sees the charge on the invoice number quoted back in the confirmation.

## What is given at the call

| Value | What it is | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_id` | the reference number of the automation service plan the charge is raised against, read from the automation service plan lookup before the call | an identifier |
| `site_id` | the reference number of the building whose controls system the work concerned, read from the building lookup or from the plan record before the call | an identifier |
| `charge_amount_usd` | the money the owner is being invoiced for the uncovered support work | in USD, recorded positive and to 2 decimal places; the settled figure only, never a range and never an expression |

## What comes back

A confirmation sentence in plain text naming the booked history entry's reference, the invoice number the line was raised on, the amount in USD to two decimal places, the calendar month the line is periodised to, the plan it was charged to and the balance now owed under the plan. The sentence being returned at all is what indicates the charge was booked; no separate status flag is sent back.

## Contract questions

**Is the balance under the plan affected by the call?** Yes: what the owner owes under that plan rises by exactly the amount invoiced.

**Does the entry carry a period of its own?** Yes: the line is periodised to the calendar month in which it is raised, and that month is named in the confirmation.
